tikas.simpleEn: The un-bolter of mantras — what removes the curse-bolt blocking mantra success — that Saptashatī hymn must be fully known. Yet one constantly busy in other mantras' chanting besides Saptashatī also reaches welfare.

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: So the chant-devoted man finds even expulsion-rites and all hard-to-get things succeeding. And to men with Saptashatī-reading missing too, by mere mantra-chanting success was already granted — now to men with mantra-chanting missing too, by mere Saptashatī-reading, He teaches every success: by this famed hymn-reading alone, the praisers win the Goddess Herself, of true-being-consciousness-bliss form — She is pleased. (Verse 3.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Besides Saptashatī-reading, other mantras' chanting also fulfils expulsion and all aims — but those who praise with this hymn-name alone win the blissful-reality Goddess Herself, by the Saptashatī alone. (Continues next.)

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: Someone may fear: if the easy Caṇḍī-praise makes all hard-won lores useless, all lores stand void. The verse answers: 'no mantra' — people hold them in contempt, so they are as if cut off, that is the feeling. 'Without' joins with mantra and the rest. (Verse 4.)

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: For that man's success no other mantra is of use, no herb, no other means like yoga-powers at all — yet without any mantra-chanting ritual, all expulsion rites and every wished-for work succeed by the hymn alone. So far: by Saptashatī-practice alone all welfare comes; and by other-mantra practice too all welfare comes — both paths stand proved.

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Saptashatī readers need no mantra, no herb, no other means at all. Without chanting-rituals their expulsion-rites and all aims succeed — by reading alone. (Continues next.)

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: He invited — He thought over — the people's doubt about the lore-family standing void. He shows His thinking: 'all' — once this bolt-making is done, the whole lore-family becomes good and fruitful; people fulfilled by mere Caṇḍī-praise alone may drop all duty-wealth-desire-freedom scriptures without loss. So the bolt was built by Śiva to block praise-born successes, to keep the other lores meaningful — that is the sense of all four verses (2–5).

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: 'Both these paths exist' — the people's doubt on both paths Hara first removed by inviting them, as it were — 'having invited the people' in sense. (Verse 5.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: 'Can everything really succeed by Saptashatī alone, with no other chanting?' — holding this doubt of people's minds before Him (calling all people), Lord Śiva thought it over… (decides next).

tikas.author: Pāṭhabheda-ṭippaṇī
tikas.simpleEn: Variant: some read 'they succeed'.

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: The Caṇḍikā hymn He made secret — unspread, hidden; though by some spreading it may be gained with effort, yet that merit's endlessness — its fruit-excess without end — He also restrained, kept reined, by a hidden device. (Verse 6.)

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: Then this very Saptashatī hymn of Caṇḍikā He made top-secret — making the second path alone the essence, over the earlier mantra-chanting path, is the sense. So Mārkaṇḍeya told the old tale from the Tantras; then, teaching disciples the Saptashatī's glory, he tells Śiva's intent: the fruit born of reading this hymn never ends, ever — while mantra-chanting-born merit does end. So know exactly as it is that restraint Śiva built — the narrowing of the first path. (Verse 6.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Mahādeva made this Saptashatī hymn of Caṇḍikā secret — because other mantras' chant-born merit fades with time, while Saptashatī-reading-born merit never fades. (Continues: Śiva's ranking must be known as exact truth — next.)

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: Don't think the hymn's power is lost altogether by the lock. To one who learns the unbolting method from the guru's mouth and practises exactly so, success comes as before, needing no other lore at all — then He shows that very method: 'on the dark (fourteenth)' means in whichever month fresh earnings come, in that month — supply the rest. (Verse 7.)

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: 'He too': he too — the other-mantra chanter — if joined with this hymn's chanting, attains all welfare; so everyone should honour Saptashatī-reading above all. This also teaches: other mantras must be chanted only after reading Saptashatī, or their fruit won't come — because this hymn alone destroys whatever blocks all mantra success, which is why it was first called the un-bolter. 'Un-bolter' means the fault-form damming success; destroying it, this too earns the name by pointer-sense. And if you ask — doesn't this hymn also need nine-lettered-mantra chanting? — we say: that is only for quicker fruit, not that without it this hymn bears none; whereas without this hymn, those mantras bear none at all — that is the special point. (Verse 7.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: That (other-mantra chanting) man too attains welfare — no doubt in this. (Continues: the dark-14th/8th rite — next.)

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: 'He gives': by two verbs joined, one single rite named give-and-take is ordained — and its exact form the Guru-bolt chapter will open up. (Verse 8.)

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: But, O disciples — knowing this hymn grants unthinkable fruit to all, and all would become all-powerful, Mahādeva bolted it, says 'on the dark (fourteenth)'. On the dark 14th or 8th, composed, the worshipper offers all his rightly-earned wealth to the Goddess — 'O Goddess, from now all this wealth of mine is given by me to You' — then, to run his worldly life, he takes it back as Her grace-gift ('take this wealth as My grace'), spends it by righteous-law paths, and stays ever Hers; to him alone the Saptashatī is pleased — not otherwise. By such a success-damming bolt Mahādeva bolted it; and this bolt's secret the mystery-lore's Guru-bolt chapter shows — we shall open it ahead. (Verse 8.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Whoever offers his all in the Goddess's service — surrenders everything — and then takes it back as grace-food, on him alone She is pleased; without this, Her pleasure is not won. By such a bolt Mahādeva keeps this Saptashatī hymn bolted. (Verse 8.)

tikas.author: Pāṭhabheda-ṭippaṇī
tikas.simpleEn: Variants: some read 'he succeeds' and 'a man is born'.

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: Verses 9–10 need nothing. The act of giving-up-doubt after knowledge begins is told in 'having known': begin and renounce — not renouncing, he is destroyed, left success-less. (Verses 11–12.)

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: 'Then what is to be done?' — 'whoever unbolts Her': since it stands thus, whoever makes this Saptashatī unbolted by the above give-and-take rite and chants Her clearly — he alone becomes perfected; he alone becomes the Goddess's troop; he too — on earth, in guarding the whole world, becomes a Gandharva, the god-kind told in the great forest-book's 'his was a daughter seized by a Gandharva' line — for he is mighty to guard the whole world. (Verse 9.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: The visible fruits are told: 'roaming nowhere' — its sense is plain itself. (Verse 10.) The fault of reading without knowing such a bolt is told in 'having known': know the above bolt first, begin its removal, then read — skipping the removal, he is destroyed. And since it stands thus, the wise begin this faultless hymn only after knowing the bolt; the ruin-talk exists only to prove bolt-knowledge is a must — for casual reading too stands allowed by other sayings. 'By Her grace' means for that reason. (Verses 11–12.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Whoever unbolts this Saptashatī hymn as told and chants daily with clear voice becomes perfected — joins Her hosts — and becomes the all-world-guarding Gandharva, singer of Her glories (9). Roaming everywhere yet fearing nowhere, never seized by sudden death, and freed after death (10). So learn this unbolting process, remove it, and only then begin the Saptashatī — skipping it leaves wishes unfulfilled; hence the learned complete this hymn only after knowing it (11). And whatever luck and fortune shines in women comes only by Her grace. (Continues: so chant only after unbolting — next.)

tikas.author: Pāṭhabheda-ṭippaṇī
tikas.simpleEn: A frank caution in Hindi: the bolt-knowledge talk exists only to stress necessity — really, the Goddess's reading helps in every way, as other sayings prove.

tikas.author: Guptavatī
tikas.simpleEn: 'Softly' means unhurriedly — not in a murmur, not in the mind, for clear-voiced chanting alone is declared a must. (Verses 13–14. Thus ends the Guptavatī explanation of the Lakṣmī-bolt.)

tikas.author: Pradīpa
tikas.simpleEn: 'Softly' — within earshot of one's own ears — brings only some wealth; but loud chanting brings all of it, complete — so begin it loud. (Verse 13.) Then the sage, finishing the bolt-rite, calls out to people: supreme freedom is freedom-in-life itself — alas, how unlucky are these people! Leaving the wish-jewel and wish-cow before their eyes, they grab a worthless cowrie-shell, that is, petty other-deity worship, for their own welfare — why? (Continued next.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Chanting this hymn softly — within one's own earshot — brings small wealth; chanting loud brings all wealth complete — so begin it loud. (Verse 13.) Then the wonder of verse 14 (continues next).

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: The rule in plain words. Only wealth freshly earned by oneself (not father's earnings), after receiving the mantra, is offered on the dark 14th or 8th standing near the Goddess, naming place and time, resolving to please Her by give-and-take, chanting 'born of You' thrice with meaning, mentally laying 'kingdom, strength, treasury' at Her feet, taking it back as Her order, giving the fifth share to teacher or his sons, setting aside a fourth for the five daily sacrifices and duties, and using the rest freely as one likes. Lunar months count here; next month's offering covers this month's gains. That is give-and-take rite number one. Second: seekers come in three grades — low, middle, high — by how early in life blazing devotion wakes in them; but here is the exception — having taken the nine-lettered mantra and learnt its Vedānta-matching meaning from the teacher, the fit soul vows lifelong never-once-careless Saptashatī reading, and lives it. That vow never to drop the begun wisdom is rite number two. The Chāndogya lines prove it; the autumn and spring vows with ninth-day worship complete the yearly round — all within one's strength.
